title: DeepSeek’s annualised revenue run rate reaches $1bn, report says
excerpt: DeepSeek’s annualised revenue run rate has doubled to $1bn in a few months after an API price rise, The Information reports.
content_html:
Chinese AI lab DeepSeek is now bringing in revenue at an annualised rate of $1bn, The Information reports, more than double the under $500M it was running at a few months ago.

The report cites two people with direct knowledge of the matter, and DeepSeek has not commented.

It puts the jump down to a recent price rise and to steady demand for the company’s models.

DeepSeek warned developers in August that a sharp increase to its API prices was on the way, as the South China Morning Post reported at the time.

According to The Information, fees went up between 2.3 and 4.5 times depending on the model, and founder Liang Wenfeng told investors that customers had stayed.

A run rate takes recent earnings and projects them across a full year, so it shows momentum rather than money already in the bank.

The Information reported last month that DeepSeek earned about 475m yuan ($70.7m) in the first seven months of 2026, roughly ten times its revenue for all of 2025.

Most of that money comes from developers who pay to use DeepSeek’s models through its API. The company’s chatbot is free to use.

The revenue figure arrives as DeepSeek nears the end of its second funding round. The Information says the company is finalising a raise of $7.5bn, a round that Bloomberg has put at a valuation of about 500bn yuan, or $74bn.

That round has not run smoothly. DeepSeek paused it in July after leaked remarks by Liang went viral on Chinese social media, then restarted talks in August.

The lab only began taking outside money this year. It closed its first round, of roughly $7bn, in June, with Liang himself providing a large share of the cash.
